content.summary: Guidance on risk stratification of suspected or confirmed pulmonary embolism (PE), emphasizing use of haemodynamic status, clinical prediction rules (PESI/sPESI), imaging assessment of right ventricle (RV) dysfunction, and laboratory cardiac biomarkers (eg, troponin) to refine prognosis and classify intermediate-risk patients.

meta_analysis.interpretation: RV dysfunction and elevated cardiac biomarkers were associated with increased risk of death; patients with signs of RV dysfunction or elevated cardiac biomarkers should be classified into intermediate–high/low-risk categories even if PESI or sPESI indicate low risk.

recommendations_highlights: Initial risk stratification of suspected or confirmed PE should be based on haemodynamic instability to identify patients at high risk of early mortality.
In haemodynamically stable patients, further stratify into intermediate and low-risk categories using clinical prediction rules integrating PE severity and comorbidity (eg, PESI or sPESI).
Assessment of the RV by imaging methods or laboratory biomarkers should be considered even when PESI is low or sPESI is negative.
Use of validated scores combining clinical, imaging, and laboratory PE-related prognostic factors may be considered to further stratify severity of the acute PE episode.
None of the commonly used prognostic scores have been validated in randomized controlled trials to date; most evidence comes from observational cohort studies.
content.evidence_limitations: Prognostic scores listed in Supplementary Data Table 4 are most frequently investigated in observational cohort studies; no randomized controlled trial validation. Heterogeneity in studies and endpoints noted.
